note: Seeded market profiles for screening only. Compiled from general industry knowledge as of early 2026 — every fact requires verification against primary sources (utility filings, county code, session law) before client reliance. That verification IS the paid product.
score_legend: 1-10 per factor, higher is better for the developer. Composite is weighted: power 35%, entitlement 20%, water 15%, incentives 15%, political 15%.

markets.name: Loudoun County, VA (Data Center Alley)
markets.profile: The densest data center market on earth. Unmatched fiber and ecosystem, but transmission constraints, multi-year delivery timelines for new large loads, and a county that no longer needs to say yes.
markets.power_outlook: Dominion has publicly flagged multi-year waits for large new loads in eastern Loudoun; new transmission lines are under development and contested. Expect energization quotes of 4-7 years for greenfield large load. Large-load tariff/rate design proceedings active.
markets.zoning_posture: County removed by-right status for data centers in most districts (2023 ZOAM); special exception now typically required, with heightened design/noise standards. Board increasingly selective.
markets.water: Loudoun Water experienced with reclaimed supply for data centers; water is rarely the binding constraint here.
markets.incentives: Virginia sales tax exemption for data center equipment (investment + jobs thresholds; extended subject to conditions). County BPOL and personal property taxes on computer equipment are significant but predictable — the tax base is why supervisors tolerate the asset class.
watch_items: Dominion large-load tariff design and PJM capacity cost pass-through
Transmission line routing fights (overhead vs underground) adding delay
GA legislation conditioning the sales tax exemption on ratepayer/energy terms
Citizen opposition now organized and experienced
markets.best_for: Operators who already hold capacity or queue position; infill/redevelopment plays; buyers of existing shells.
markets.avoid_if: You need speed-to-power on greenfield. The market's moat is now its constraint.

markets.name: Phoenix Metro / Maricopa County, AZ
markets.profile: Top-tier growth market: cheap flat land, low natural disaster risk, two sophisticated utilities. Water politics and summer peak constraints are the story.
markets.power_outlook: APS and SRP both managing heavy data center queues; multi-year timelines for 100MW+ but generally better than PJM East. Both utilities developing large-load rate structures and requiring significant financial commitments.
markets.zoning_posture: Generally accommodating in industrial corridors (Mesa, Goodyear, Buckeye, Chandler legacy sites). Some municipalities tightening design and noise standards; Tucson-area pushback has been louder than Phoenix proper.
markets.water: The headline risk. Active Management Area rules constrain groundwater; assured water supply requirements affect some structures. Air-cooled or closed-loop designs plus municipal/reclaimed supply are the viable path — evaporative designs face real scrutiny.
markets.incentives: Arizona TPT (sales) exemption for qualifying data center equipment via ACA certification; 10-20 year terms depending on investment level.
watch_items: Groundwater/AMA policy developments and municipal water-service moratorium areas
Large-load tariff dockets at the ACC
Grid interconnection with planned new generation (gas + storage) timing
markets.best_for: Hyperscale campuses with air-cooled designs and patience for utility-scale negotiation.
markets.avoid_if: Your design needs heavy evaporative cooling from groundwater.

markets.name: Central Ohio (Columbus / New Albany / Licking County)
markets.profile: The Midwest's breakout market — hyperscaler campuses, Intel adjacency, aggressive local economic development. The AEP large-load tariff fight made it the national test case for data center rate design.
markets.power_outlook: AEP Ohio's data center tariff (PUCO-approved settlement) imposes long-term minimum demand charges and exit obligations on large new loads — financeable but must be modeled. Queue is heavy; timelines stretching but better than NoVA.
markets.zoning_posture: New Albany International Business Park is the template — pre-entitled, utility-coordinated. Outside the established corridors, townships vary widely and some have grown skeptical.
markets.water: Generally adequate via municipal systems; Columbus regional water planning has kept pace. Not the binding constraint.
markets.incentives: Ohio sales tax exemption for qualifying data centers (Tax Credit Authority approval); CRA/enterprise zone property tax abatements negotiated locally; New Albany-style 100% abatements with school district revenue-sharing are the pattern.
watch_items: AEP tariff terms as precedent — and copycat filings in other states
Licking County growth-pains politics (roads, farmland conversion)
School district compensation expectations rising
markets.best_for: Hyperscale and large colo following the established corridor playbook.
markets.avoid_if: Pro forma can't carry the tariff's minimum-demand floor through a slow ramp.

markets.name: Dallas–Fort Worth, TX
markets.profile: Scale, speed, and a deregulated market that lets sophisticated buyers structure power creatively. ERCOT's large-load interconnection reforms (SB 6 era) introduced new rules of the road.
markets.power_outlook: Oncor queue is enormous but Texas builds. SB 6 (2025) added large-load registration, curtailment-during-emergency frameworks, and cost-allocation provisions — know them before promising firm capacity. Behind-the-meter and co-located generation deals are viable here like nowhere else.
markets.zoning_posture: City-by-city; unincorporated areas have minimal zoning (but watch ETJ dynamics). Fort Worth/Alliance corridor and south Dallas industrial belts are well-trodden. Municipal design standards tightening modestly.
markets.water: Generally available via municipal systems; North Texas districts planning for growth. Evaporative designs feasible but reclaimed supply increasingly smart politics.
markets.incentives: Texas data center sales tax exemption (investment/jobs thresholds); Chapter 312 abatements and JETI (Ch. 403) for qualifying projects; no state income tax. Property tax base is high, making abatement negotiation central.
watch_items: ERCOT large-load interconnection rule implementation
Legislative interest in data center water and grid impacts
Appraisal district aggressiveness on data center valuations
markets.best_for: Speed-to-market builds; operators comfortable with ERCOT market risk and curtailment frameworks.
markets.avoid_if: Tenant requires firm, non-curtailable power with zero market exposure and you can't structure around ERCOT emergency rules.

markets.name: Atlanta Metro, GA
markets.profile: Fiber-rich, fast-growing, and newly contested. Atlanta proper restricted data centers near transit; the legislature has fought over the sales tax exemption; Georgia Power is rebuilding its resource plan around data center load.
markets.power_outlook: Georgia Power's IRP updates added major capacity for data center demand; PSC approved large-load tariff provisions shifting infrastructure risk to large customers. Timelines moderate; utility is motivated but commission scrutiny is high.
markets.zoning_posture: City of Atlanta restricted data centers in core districts/BeltLine areas; suburban and exurban counties (Douglas, Fayette, Coweta, Bartow) range from welcoming to newly skeptical — several adopted pauses or tightened standards.
markets.water: Metro water wars history makes large withdrawals sensitive; municipal supply generally workable with closed-loop designs.
markets.incentives: State sales tax exemption for high-tech data center equipment — politically contested (suspension attempts, conditions debated). Local abatements via development authorities (bond-lease structures) are standard practice.
watch_items: Legislative attempts to suspend/condition the sales tax exemption
Georgia Power large-load tariff implementation and PSC elections
County-level moratorium contagion in the exurbs
markets.best_for: Operators with strong community-engagement playbooks targeting pre-zoned industrial corridors.
markets.avoid_if: Underwriting assumes the sales tax exemption survives unchanged through multiple refresh cycles.

markets.name: Central Washington (Quincy / Grant, Douglas & Chelan Counties)
markets.profile: Hydro-powered legacy market with some of the cheapest, cleanest power in North America — but PUD capacity is largely spoken for and new allocations are rationed. The lawyer-builder's home-turf advantage market.
markets.power_outlook: PUD rates remain enviable but headroom is constrained; new large-load requests face allocation policies, higher 'evolving industry' rate classes, and queue discipline. BPA regional capacity and new transmission are the long-term unlock.
markets.zoning_posture: Quincy and Grant County remain practically accommodating (data centers are the tax base); permitting is navigable. SEPA review applies — schedule it, don't fear it.
markets.water: Columbia Basin supply with municipal/industrial allocations; Quincy has history with reclaimed/cooling solutions. Far better than Phoenix; still paper it carefully.
markets.incentives: Washington rural-county data center sales/use tax exemption (eligibility windows and certification requirements have shifted repeatedly — verify current program status and sunset). No state income tax; B&O and REET planning matter on the deal itself.
watch_items: Legislative renewal/modification of the rural data center exemption
PUD large-load rate class and allocation policy changes
CETA (clean energy) compliance interactions with new load
markets.best_for: Operators who can win a PUD allocation or buy an existing powered site; ESG-driven tenants paying up for hydro.
markets.avoid_if: You need 100MW+ of new allocation on a near-term schedule.

markets.name: Des Moines Metro / Council Bluffs, IA
markets.profile: Hyperscaler favorite: wind-heavy generation, low rates, genuinely fast government, and incentives that have survived politics. Less fiber density than coastal markets but the big platforms solved that themselves.
markets.power_outlook: MidAmerican's wind fleet and constructive regulatory climate keep timelines among the best in the country for committed large loads. MISO queue reform applies but utility-led solutions are common.
markets.zoning_posture: Altoona, West Des Moines, Council Bluffs: practiced, fast, predictable. Greenfield annexation/rezoning timelines measured in months, not years.
markets.water: Adequate municipal supply; some scrutiny rising on large users but nothing like the Southwest.
markets.incentives: Iowa sales tax exemption for qualifying data centers; property tax abatements/TIF locally negotiated; utility economic development riders available.
watch_items: MISO capacity market tightening
Incentive threshold updates in the legislature
Competition for sites near existing hyperscale campuses
markets.best_for: Hyperscale build-to-suit; anyone prioritizing execution certainty over network density.
markets.avoid_if: Multi-tenant colo needing dense interconnection ecosystems.

markets.name: Northern Nevada (Reno / TRIC / Storey County)
markets.profile: Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center is the fastest entitlement story in America — pre-approved industrial land at scale. Power and water are the gating items; Nevada's incentive program is strong.
markets.power_outlook: NV Energy managing rapid large-load growth; major new transmission (Greenlink) under construction with multi-year horizons. Large-load tariff/contract structures (special contracts approved by PUCN) are the norm for 50MW+.
markets.zoning_posture: TRIC/Storey County: industrial use effectively by-right with administrative review — weeks, not years. Washoe County more conventional.
markets.water: High desert: water rights are bought, not assumed. TRIC has dedicated supply infrastructure but large evaporative designs need careful rights diligence; effluent reuse deals are the local pattern.
markets.incentives: Nevada data center abatement program (sales tax to ~2%, property tax abatements for 10-20 yrs with investment/jobs thresholds via GOED). No corporate income tax.
watch_items: Greenlink transmission schedule and cost allocation
PUCN large-load docket activity
Water rights market pricing in the Truckee Meadows basin
markets.best_for: Speed-obsessed builds that can phase power; crypto-to-AI conversions; operators with water rights strategy.
